totals.simulated_games_note: Sum of matchups.games in the lab results database at export time: ALL campaigns and BOTH patches 1.21 and 1.22, so it is not the number behind the 1.22 results (see patch_games); grows while the lab runs.
totals.patch_games_note: Games counted by the funnel for patch 1.22: finals + round_robin + halving + screen. The extra round-robin deck's 1,536 games are real patch 1.22 games but are NOT included (see patch_games_extra_deck).

methodology.headline: The patch 1.22 rankings come from about 1.15 million simulated matches played by search AIs in an offline copy of the game (Monte Carlo rollouts with a simulated shop).
methodology.withheld_note: The deck ranked 1 in the tier list is withheld by the maintainer until a balance patch: its numbers are published, its cards are not. The lab measured 4,868 decks; decks.json lists 4,816. Every measured deck, listed or not, is counted in the totals and in the fields the other decks were measured against.
methodology.settings: Patch 1.22. Decks are played without talents. Draws count as half a win.

pipeline.description: Basic AI, every candidate deck against 54 reference decks, 4 games each (216 games per deck).
Strong AI against 8 probe decks in three rounds (24, then 72, then 168 games cumulative); the best and a capped rescue of promising decks go on.
Strong AI, the 48 best decks play each other, 32 games per pair.
Strong AI, the top 10 decks, 200 games per pair.

cross_check.description: The top decks were cross-checked by an AlphaZero-style AI from a second PC (neural networks plus tree search, trained by self-play), which reproduced the same winner and top 4.

limits: Results describe play by search AIs, not human players; matchup knowledge and skill can change the picture.

Ranks 11-30 are ordered by their win rate against the top 10 (320 games each, about ±5 points), so neighbours a few points apart are not ranked apart with confidence. Their results against the other good decks are shown beside them as a second number.
The finals ordering (ranks 1-10) is better separated at the top only (see the 95% intervals).
